title: Wall-Mount Hose Reels and Lighter Hoses: A Tidier Way to Water the Garden
subtitle: A wall-mount reel gives your hose a home, and a different kind of hose may handle better, though neither does the watering for you.
excerpt: Here is how wall-mount hose reels and hybrid hoses work, what they cost, and what they cannot fix.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: A garden hose is simple, until it is not. It kinks halfway to the tomatoes, tangles into a heap by the back door, and has to be coiled by hand every time you finish. For many of us, the bending and pulling is what makes watering feel like a chore.

Two fairly modest purchases may help. A wall-mount hose reel gives the hose a tidy home next to the outdoor faucet and lets you wind it up with a crank. A different type of hose may be easier to handle on the way across the yard. This setup suits homes with an outdoor spigot and a solid wall nearby. If you rent or have no yard, it may not be the right fit.

The reel is a drum on a bracket that you fasten to the house. A short connector hose, called a leader hose, runs from your faucet to the reel. Your main hose attaches to the reel, and you turn a handle to wind it in or let it out.

It helps to be clear about what a reel does not do. It only rewinds the hose. It does not make a 100-foot hose any lighter to pull across the lawn, and it will not fix kinks that are already in the hose. That is why the hose itself matters as much as the reel.
Hoses come in different materials. Consumer Reports advises that inexpensive vinyl hoses are for lighter jobs, and says:
"Most vinyl hoses are best suited to light garden work and washing cars."
Hybrid polymer hoses cost more. The Flexzilla hose below, for example, is described by its seller as lightweight and easy to handle, and as not kinking under pressure.

items: Length and width: Consumer Reports suggests a hose of at least 100 feet that is at least 5/8 inch wide. Make sure your reel is made for that size. The guidance comes from a Consumer Reports article whose date we could not confirm.
Sturdy materials: Consumer Reports says a metal or heavy-duty plastic reel is more durable, and advises looking for brass fittings on the hose.
Total cost: neither Suncast reel below includes a hose. Add the price of both before you decide.
Mounting hardware: fasteners are not included with the Suncast reels. The Suncast manual says the supplied screws are for wood siding, and other walls need other fasteners.

The crank: if your hands are stiff, try turning a reel by hand before buying. One buyer review described a stiff crank and a short handle, which is a single opinion, not a test. The 100 ft Suncast model comes with an extended crank handle.
Winter storage: both Suncast reels are listed with a removable reel for winter storage.
Returns and warranty: confirm both on the order page, since no warranty appeared on the listings we reviewed.

sections.content: Putting it up and using it well

Mounting a reel takes a drill, the right fasteners for your wall and sometimes a ladder. If you are at all unsteady on your feet, skip the ladder and ask someone to help. This is a good small job for a family member, a neighbor or a handyman.
Once it is up, take your time winding the hose in. When cold weather comes, the Suncast reels can be removed for winter storage.

The Zoro listings for both Suncast reels say the hose and the mounting fasteners are not included. If you pair the 100-foot Suncast reel ($42.49) with the 100-foot Flexzilla hose ($89.99), expect to spend roughly $130 to $140 before fasteners and shipping, based on November 2026 prices. Zoro is a supplier aimed at businesses, and free shipping over $50 requires signing in. Prices change, so check before you order. For comparison, an HGTV summary lists a Giraffe Tools retractable wall-mount reel at $179.99, with hardware not included. We have not seen the full page, so recheck that price.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: A reel on the wall and a hose that handles well will not do the gardening for you, but they can make the hose easier to put away. Take it one step at a time, and ask for a hand with the mounting.

products.name: Suncast 100 ft Sidewinder Wall Mount Hose Reel (SWA100)
products.blurb: A fully assembled resin reel for a 100-foot, 5/8-inch hose, with an extended crank handle and a 6-foot leader hose. The reel is removable for winter storage; hose and mounting fasteners are sold separately.

products.name: Suncast 125 ft Side Tracker Wall Mount Hose Reel (STA125B)
products.blurb: Holds up to 125 feet of 5/8-inch hose, with a hose guide for winding and a 5-foot leader hose. It measures 21.5 inches tall and 19 inches wide; hose and fasteners are not included.

products.name: Flexzilla SwivelGrip 5/8 in x 100 ft Garden Hose
products.blurb: A hybrid polymer hose that Ace describes as lightweight and easy to handle, with ends that swivel to release coils and a large grip surface for tight connections. Ace says it lays flat, does not kink under pressure and is drinking water safe.
